86	  and pure. Callers own retry loops and timeout semantics.
87	- **Full retry implementation** — michi provides `RetryConfig`,
88	  `parse_retry_after()`, and `next_retry_delay()`. The actual retry loop
89	  (sleep + re-execute) stays in the caller.
90	- **Caching** — callers should use `moka` or equivalent. michi does not
91	  include a cache.
92	- **Logging / telemetry** — Rust consumers use the `tracing` crate
93	  independently.
94	- **Schema validation** — input validation is the caller's concern.
95	- **MCP server bootstrapping** — `server.tool()`, tool discovery, deferred
96	  loading. Protocol-specific, stays in your MCP SDK.
97	
98	---
99	
100	## Consumer map
101	
102	```
103	Any Rust CLI binary
104	  Cargo.toml dep on michi (crates.io or git)
105	  Render --format toon via michi::render_toon()
106	  Full access to all modules — no NAPI overhead
107	
108	Any TypeScript CLI
109	  npm dep on michi
110	  --format toon dispatch calls into NAPI wrapper
111	  Same output; NAPI boundary is transparent
112	
113	Any TypeScript MCP server
114	  npm dep on michi
115	  Renders TOON for audience:["assistant"] content block
116	  Assembles MCP content[] from the returned string
117	```
118	
119	---
120	
121	## Cargo.toml
122	
123	```toml
124	[package]
125	name = "michi"
126	version = "0.1.0"
127	edition = "2021"
128	rust-version = "1.93"
129	description = "AXI response primitives for agent-ergonomic tools"
130	license = "AGPL-3.0-or-later"
131	repository = "https://github.com/orin-axi/michi"
132	keywords = ["axi", "agent", "mcp", "cli", "llm"]
133	categories = ["text-processing", "encoding", "development-tools"]
134	
135	[features]
136	default = []
137	napi    = ["dep:napi", "dep:napi-derive"]
138	cli     = []  # reserved: terminal-width-aware rendering, colour support
139	
140	[dependencies]
141	serde      = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
142	serde_json = "1"
143	thiserror  = "2"
144	
145	[dependencies.napi]
146	version  = "2"
147	features = ["napi4"]
148	optional = true
149	
150	[dependencies.napi-derive]
151	version  = "2"
152	optional = true
153	
154	[build-dependencies.napi-build]
155	version  = "1"
156	optional = true
157	
158	[dev-dependencies]
159	criterion = { version = "0.5", features = ["html_reports"] }
160	proptest  = "1"
161	insta     = { version = "1", features = ["yaml"] }
162	
163	[[bench]]
164	name    = "toon_render"
165	harness = false
166	
167	[[bench]]
168	name    = "kv_render"
169	harness = false
170	```
171	
172	The `napi = { features = ["napi4"] }` selection is deliberate — `napi4` is the
173	lowest Node-API level that exposes `ThreadsafeFunction` and the async machinery
174	napi-rs needs. See the NAPI section for the full rationale.
175	
176	---
177	
178	## Crate layout
179	
180	```
181	michi/
182	  Cargo.toml
183	  build.rs                      # napi-build (conditional on napi feature)
184	  src/
185	    lib.rs                      # public API, re-exports, crate-level docs
186	    toon/
187	      mod.rs                    # render_toon(), ToonOptions, Value
188	      escape.rs                 # comma/quote/null escaping
189	      render.rs                 # string assembly with pre-allocated capacity
190	    kv/
191	      mod.rs                    # render_kv(), KvItem, KvValue
192	    hints.rs                    # Hint, render_hints(), append_hints()
193	    truncate.rs                 # Truncated, truncate(), truncate_inline()
194	    empty.rs                    # empty_state(), empty_state_with_hints()
195	    error.rs                    # AxiError, ErrorCode
196	    idempotency.rs              # IdempotencyKey, already_done(), PartialSuccess
197	    resilience.rs               # RetryConfig, parse_retry_after(), next_retry_delay()
198	    status.rs                   # StatusItem, StatusResponse, Health
199	    recovery.rs                 # RecoveryHint, render_recovery()

200	    response.rs                 # AgentResponse builder, OutputFormat
201	    napi.rs                     # #[napi] exports (napi feature only)
202	  benches/
203	    toon_render.rs
204	    kv_render.rs
205	  tests/
206	    toon_integration.rs
207	    kv_integration.rs
208	    resilience_integration.rs
209	    idempotency_integration.rs
210	    snapshot_tests.rs           # insta snapshots
211	
212	packages/michi-node/            # NAPI wrapper (npm: michi)
213	  Cargo.toml                    # napi feature, napi-rs build
214	  package.json                  # name: "michi"
215	  index.js                      # platform binary loader + TS fallback
216	  index.d.ts                    # TypeScript types (auto-generated)
217	  src/
218	    lib.rs                      # #[napi] exports wrapping crate functions
219	  __test__/
220	    index.test.mjs              # Jest NAPI integration tests
221	```
222	
223	---
224	
225	## TOON format specification
226	
227	TOON (Token-Optimized Object Notation) is the agent-facing list format.
228	It front-loads structure (type, count, field names) so the LLM has full
229	context before reading any row, then encodes rows as compact comma-separated
230	values. Field names appear once in the header rather than once per row.
231	
232	This is the canonical implementation of **AXI Principle 1 (Token-Efficient
233	Output)**: every token in a response permanently consumes context-window
234	budget, and on multi-turn tasks that cost compounds across turns. TOON omits
235	the braces, quotes, and repeated keys that JSON spends on structure the LLM can
236	already infer positionally.
237	
238	**Why TOON for lists?**
239	Standard JSON repeats field names on every item. Markdown key-value format
240	repeats field names per item, which is ideal for single items and small sets
241	but expensive at scale. TOON trades per-item field repetition for a one-time
242	header, saving proportionally more tokens as N grows. For lists of 5+ items,
243	TOON is the better token budget choice. For single items or small metadata
244	blocks, key-value format remains preferred — see `kv::render_kv()`.
245	
246	AXI's benchmark shows this class of output optimization delivers approximately
247	40% token reduction over equivalent JSON for list data.
248	
249	### Grammar
250	
251	```
252	document     ::= type_header NEWLINE row+ totalcount? help_block?
253	type_header  ::= type_name "[" count "]" "{" field_list "}" ":"
254	type_name    ::= [a-z_][a-z0-9_]*                 (snake_case)
255	count        ::= [0-9]+                            (items in this response)
256	field_list   ::= field_name ("," field_name)*
257	field_name   ::= [a-z_][a-z0-9_]*
258	row          ::= "  " value ("," value)* NEWLINE   (2-space indent)
259	value        ::= scalar | quoted
260	scalar       ::= [^,\n"]*
261	quoted       ::= '"' ( [^"\\] | "\\" . )* '"'     (for values with commas)
262	totalcount   ::= "totalCount: " [0-9]+ NEWLINE     (total available, may exceed count)
263	help_block   ::= "help[" [0-9]+ "]:" NEWLINE hint+
264	hint         ::= "  " [^\n]+ NEWLINE
265	```
266	
267	### Examples
268	
269	**List response:**
270	```
271	issues[3]{number,title,state}:
272	  42,Fix login redirect,open
273	  43,Add dark mode,open
274	  44,"Update deps, bump major",closed
275	totalCount: 47
276	help[2]:
277	  Call get_issue with number=<number> for full detail
278	  Call list_issues with state=open to filter
279	```
280	
281	**Truncated field value:**
282	```
283	components[2]{name,description,tokens}:
284	  Button,"Primary action element (148 chars truncated — use full=true)",12
285	  Icon,"Scalable vector icon (203 chars truncated — use full=true)",8
286	totalCount: 84
287	help[1]:
288	  Call get_component with name=<name> and full=true for complete description
289	```
290	
291	**Empty state:**
292	```
293	issues[0]{}:
294	totalCount: 0
295	help[1]:
296	  Try list_issues with a broader filter
297	```

# michi — Architecture Design
> orin-axi · 2026-07-03

This document records the architectural decisions made during the July 2026
brainstorming session. It supersedes and extends any open questions in
`01-spec.md` (which predates this session). Implementation plans should treat
this doc as authoritative on the topics it covers.

---

## 1. One crate, feature-gated

**Decision: one `michi` crate with optional features. No separate execution crate.**

The original spec positioned michi as a pure sync rendering library with no
async runtime. The question was whether pipeline execution (tokio, moka, nucleo)
should live in a companion crate (`kata`) or in michi itself behind features.

Feature gates give the same guarantee that crate boundaries give — a consumer
who adds `michi` with default features pulls in zero tokio, zero moka, zero
nucleo. The "pure computation" principle is enforced by cargo, not by convention.

The suite tools (Monokl, Firkin, Lumen, Pulse) all need both rendering primitives
and pipeline execution. One crate means one dep, one version pin, one mental model.
Two crates would require cross-crate type conversions and coordinated releases with
no architectural benefit.

The NAPI wrapper (`packages/michi-node`) remains a separate Cargo crate because
`crate-type = ["cdylib"]` cannot coexist with a regular `[lib]` in one
`Cargo.toml`. This is a build-artifact boundary, not a conceptual one.

---

## 2. Feature taxonomy

```toml
[features]
default  = []

# Async execution layer: PipelineExecutor, Step, CheckpointStore, OutputSink,
# CircuitBreaker, with_resilience(). Adds: tokio, tokio-util, async-trait,
# thiserror, uuid.
pipeline = [
    "dep:tokio",
    "dep:tokio-util",
    "dep:async-trait",
    "dep:uuid",
]

# Fuzzy matching: FuzzyMatcher, FuzzyResolver, Disambiguator trait.
# Implies pipeline (Resolution<T> is used in pipeline context).
# Adds: nucleo-matcher.
fuzzy = ["dep:nucleo-matcher", "pipeline"]

# Two-tier cache: moka async LRU + disk LRU with tag invalidation +
# stale-while-revalidate. Adds: moka, sha2.
cache = ["dep:moka", "dep:sha2", "pipeline"]

# CLI surface adapter: CliSink (indicatif spinners), DiskCheckpointStore,
# TtyDisambiguator, install_ctrl_c_handler.
# Adds: indicatif, inquire, crossterm, ctrlc, atty.
cli = [
    "dep:indicatif",
    "dep:inquire",
    "dep:crossterm",
    "dep:ctrlc",
    "dep:atty",
    "pipeline",
]

# MCP surface adapter: McpSink, MemoryCheckpointStore, McpDisambiguator.
# Pure logic — no additional non-tokio deps.
mcp = ["pipeline"]

# NAPI npm wrapper surface. Used by packages/michi-node only.
napi = ["dep:napi", "dep:napi-derive"]

# Everything except napi (napi is build-artifact-level, not feature-level).
full = ["pipeline", "fuzzy", "cache", "cli", "mcp"]
```

Typical consumer configs:

| Consumer | Features |
|---|---|
| Pure rendering (Rust CLI, no pipeline) | `michi` (defaults) |
| Rust CLI that runs pipelines | `michi = { features = ["cli"] }` |
| TypeScript MCP server via npm | `michi` npm package (default) |
| MCP server that runs pipelines | `michi = { features = ["mcp"] }` |
| Test/bench harness | `michi = { features = ["full"] }` |
| `packages/michi-node` Cargo.toml | `michi = { features = ["napi"] }` |

---

## 3. Module map

Modules in the left column are always compiled (default features). Modules in
the right column are gated.

```
src/
  lib.rs

  ── Always compiled ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  toon/
    mod.rs          render_toon(), ToonOptions, Value
    escape.rs       comma/quote/null escaping
    render.rs       string assembly with pre-allocated capacity

  kv/
    mod.rs          render_kv(), KvItem, KvValue

  hints.rs          Hint, render_hints(), append_hints()
  truncate.rs       Truncated, truncate(), truncate_inline()
  empty.rs          empty_state(), empty_state_with_hints()
  error.rs          Error (unified — see §4), ErrorClass, Sensitive<T>
  idempotency.rs    IdempotencyKey, already_done(), PartialSuccess
  recovery.rs       RecoveryHint, render_recovery()
  status.rs         StatusItem, StatusResponse, Health
  response.rs       AgentResponse builder, OutputFormat

  resilience/
    mod.rs          RetryConfig, next_retry_delay(), parse_retry_after()  ← always
    policy.rs       with_resilience()                                      ← pipeline
    circuit.rs      CircuitBreaker, CircuitState                          ← pipeline

  pipeline/
    mod.rs          Pipeline (pure data type + render())                   ← always
    executor.rs     PipelineExecutor, PipelineContext                     ← pipeline
    step.rs         Step, StepFn, StepContext, SkipReason                 ← pipeline
    graph.rs        assign_levels(), cycle detection                      ← pipeline
    result.rs       PipelineResult, RunStatus                             ← pipeline
    checkpoint.rs   Checkpoint, CheckpointStore, NoopCheckpointStore      ← pipeline

  sink/
    mod.rs          OutputSink, AgentEvent, NoopSink                      ← pipeline

  telemetry/
    mod.rs          TelemetryProvider, NoopProvider                       ← always (zero-cost)

  ── Optional features ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  fuzzy/
    mod.rs          FuzzyMatcher, FuzzyResolver, Resolution<T>            ← fuzzy
    matcher.rs      nucleo-matcher wrapper, MatcherConfig                 ← fuzzy
    resolver.rs     Disambiguator trait, resolve()                        ← fuzzy

  cache/
    mod.rs          Cache, CachePolicy, CacheEntry                        ← cache
    memory.rs       moka::future::Cache wrapper                           ← cache
    disk.rs         DiskCache, tag invalidation                           ← cache
    policy.rs       CachePolicyBuilder, stale-while-revalidate            ← cache

  adapters/
    cli/
      mod.rs        CliSink, HumanWriter, JsonWriter                      ← cli
      checkpoint.rs DiskCheckpointStore                                   ← cli
      disambig.rs   TtyDisambiguator                                      ← cli
      ctrl_c.rs     install_ctrl_c_handler()                              ← cli
    mcp/
      mod.rs        McpSink                                               ← mcp
      checkpoint.rs MemoryCheckpointStore                                 ← mcp
      disambig.rs   McpDisambiguator                                      ← mcp

  napi.rs           #[napi] exports                                       ← napi
```

### Module principles

- Pure vs async split within a module: sync computation always compiled, async
  extension behind `pipeline`. Pattern from `resilience/`: `next_retry_delay()`
  is always there; `with_resilience()` requires the feature.
- `pipeline::Pipeline` (pure data type + `render()`) is always compiled because
  tools may want to render a pipeline state without executing it.
- `telemetry` uses `NoopProvider` (zero-cost impl) so it compiles clean without
  a runtime dep.

---

## 4. Error type consolidation

The original spec had `AxiError` (rendering-focused, michi) as a separate concept
from `AgentError` (infrastructure, the proposed execution spec). In a unified
crate these merge into `michi::Error`.

```rust
// src/error.rs
#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum Error {
    // ── Execution errors (pipeline feature) ───────────────────────────────
    #[error("HTTP {status}: {message}")]
    Http { status: u16, message: String, retryable: bool, retry_after: Option<Duration> },

    #[error("Timeout after {elapsed:?}")]
    Timeout { elapsed: Duration },

    #[error("Step {id} failed")]
    StepFailed { id: String, #[source] source: Box<Error> },

    #[error("Circuit {name} is open, retry after {retry_after:?}")]
    CircuitOpen { name: String, retry_after: Duration },

    #[error("No match for query: {query}")]
    NoMatch { query: String },

    #[error("Ambiguous match for {query}: {count} candidates")]
    AmbiguousMatch { query: String, count: usize },

    #[error("Cyclic dependency: {cycle:?}")]
    CyclicDependency { cycle: Vec<String> },

    #[error("Cancelled")]
    Cancelled,

    #[error("Cache error: {0}")]
    Cache(String),

    #[error(transparent)]
    Io(#[from] std::io::Error),

    // ── Domain errors (always) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
    #[error("Invalid input: {0}")]
    InvalidInput(String),

    #[error("Not found: {0}")]
    NotFound(String),
}

impl Error {
    /// Render to agent-readable stdout string (AxiError-style).
    pub fn render(&self) -> String { ... }
    pub fn exit_code(&self) -> i32 { 1 }
    pub fn class(&self) -> ErrorClass { ... }
    pub fn is_retryable(&self) -> bool { ... }
}

pub enum ErrorClass { User, Internal, Transient }

/// Wrapper that omits the inner value from Debug/Display output.
pub struct Sensitive<T>(pub T);
```

`Sensitive<T>` and `ErrorClass` are always compiled. The execution error variants
(`Http`, `Timeout`, `StepFailed`, `CircuitOpen`, `NoMatch`, `AmbiguousMatch`,
`CyclicDependency`, `Cancelled`, `Cache`) are gated behind `#[cfg(feature = "pipeline")]`.

---

## 5. Repo shape

```
michi/                          ← git root: git@github.com:orin-axi/michi.git
  Cargo.toml                    ← [workspace] members + [package] michi lib
  Cargo.lock
  rust-toolchain.toml           ← pinned stable channel
  build.rs                      ← napi-build (conditional on napi feature)
  justfile                      ← unified task runner (see §6)
  .rustfmt.toml                 ← edition=2021, max_width=120
  .clippy.toml                  ← msrv, too-many-arguments-threshold=6
  .typos.toml                   ← spell-check config
  deny.toml                     ← license + advisory + bans policy
  CLAUDE.md                     ← agent session instructions
  README.md
  src/                          ← michi lib source (as above)
  benches/
    toon_render.rs
    kv_render.rs
    pipeline_render.rs
  tests/
    toon_integration.rs
    kv_integration.rs
    resilience_integration.rs
    idempotency_integration.rs
    pipeline_integration.rs     ← pipeline feature, uses tokio::test
    snapshot_tests.rs           ← insta snapshots
  packages/
    michi-node/                 ← NAPI cdylib (separate Cargo crate, required by Rust)
      Cargo.toml                ← crate-type = ["cdylib"], deps on michi napi feature
      package.json              ← name: "michi", published to npm
      index.js                  ← platform binary loader
      index.d.ts                ← generated by napi-derive v3
      src/lib.rs                ← thin #[napi] shim over michi::*
      __test__/
        index.test.mjs
  .github/
    workflows/
      ci.yml
  docs/
    00-overview.md
    01-spec.md
    projects/
      01-mvp.md
      agents/                   ← session briefs for S0–S4
    superpowers/
      specs/
        2026-07-03-michi-design.md   ← this file
```

**Workspace Cargo.toml:**

```toml
[workspace]
members = [
    ".",
    "packages/michi-node",
]
resolver = "2"

[workspace.package]
edition     = "2021"
rust-version = "1.96"
license     = "AGPL-3.0-or-later"
repository  = "https://github.com/orin-axi/michi"
authors     = ["orin-axi"]

[profile.release]
opt-level      = 3
lto            = "thin"
codegen-units  = 1

[profile.bench]
inherits = "release"
debug    = true
```

No pnpm workspace root for v0.1 (one JS package, no cross-package hoisting
needed). Add `pnpm-workspace.yaml` when a second JS package joins the repo.

---

## 6. Tooling stack

| Tool | Role | Version |
|---|---|---|
| `just` | Unified local task runner | latest |
| `cargo nextest` | Parallel test runner (replaces `cargo test`) | via taiki-e/install-action |
| `cargo-llvm-cov` | Coverage → lcov → Codecov | via taiki-e/install-action |
| `cargo-deny` | License + advisory + ban policy | latest |
| `divan` | Benchmarks (not criterion) | 0.1 |
| `insta` | Snapshot tests | 1, yaml feature |
| `typos` | Spell-check | latest |
| `pnpm` | JS package manager for michi-node | 9+ |
| `@napi-rs/cli` | NAPI build + publish tooling | 3 |
| `napi` / `napi-derive` | NAPI bindings | **3** (not 2) |

**Not used:**
- `criterion` — divan is the benchmark crate (consistent with oxc-react-codegen)
- `rayon` — pure sync rendering has no parallelism to exploit at the crate level
- `miette` — callers own error display; michi's error type focuses on agent rendering
- Moon — repo is too small; two crates don't need a polyglot task graph
- tokio in default features — execution layer is always opt-in via `pipeline` feature

### justfile (canonical tasks)

```justfile
default:
    @just --list

# ── Build ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
build:
    cargo build --workspace

build-release:
    cargo build --release --workspace

build-node:
    cd packages/michi-node && pnpm build --platform

build-node-release:
    cd packages/michi-node && pnpm build --platform --release

# ── Test ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
test: test-rust test-node

test-rust:
    cargo nextest run --workspace

test-rust-all:
    cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features

test-node: build-node
    cd packages/michi-node && pnpm test

# ── Lint ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
check: fmt-check clippy deny typos

fmt:
    cargo fmt --all

fmt-check:
    cargo fmt --all --check

clippy:
    cargo clippy --workspace --all-features -- -D warnings

deny:
    cargo deny check

typos:
    typos

# ── Snapshots ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
snapshots:
    cargo insta review

# ── Benchmarks ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
bench:
    cargo bench --workspace

# ── Coverage ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
coverage:
    cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --all-features --lcov --output-path lcov.info

# ── Pre-push ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ci: check test
```

CI (GitHub Actions) uses raw cargo/pnpm commands directly — no `just` dep in CI.

---

## 7. Spec updates required in 01-spec.md

These items in the existing spec are now outdated and should be corrected during
implementation:

| Location | Current (wrong) | Correct |
|---|---|---|
| `Cargo.toml` `[dependencies.napi]` | `version = "2"` | `version = "3"` |
| `Cargo.toml` `[dependencies.napi-derive]` | `version = "2"` | `version = "3"` |
| `Cargo.toml` `[dev-dependencies]` | `criterion = { version = "0.5" }` | `divan = "0.1"` |
| `[features]` | `napi`, `cli = []` only | Full feature taxonomy (see §2) |
| Non-goals | "zero tokio, zero async-std" | True for default features; `pipeline` feature adds tokio |
| Consumer map | No pipeline mention | Add pipeline execution consumer shape |
| `error.rs` | `AxiError, ErrorCode` | `Error` (unified), `ErrorClass`, `Sensitive<T>` |
| `[[bench]]` | `harness = false` under criterion | divan bench setup |

---

## 8. Open questions (not blocking v0.1)

**Q1 — MSRV:** Set to 1.96 in workspace (matching oxc-react-codegen pattern).
Verify no dep requires higher before first publish.

**Q2 — disk cache path:** `DiskCache` needs a path at construction. CLI adapter
uses `~/.cache/michi/`. MCP adapter uses temp dir. Injected by the caller —
michi provides no default path discovery.

**Q3 — AGPL vs MIT/Apache:** Spec says AGPL-3.0-or-later. Confirm with project
owner before publish. AGPL requires source disclosure for network use, which may
affect suite tool consumers.

**Q4 — `napi4` feature level:** Spec historically chose `napi4` for
ThreadsafeFunction. With NAPI v3 and the sync-only default feature set, verify
the minimum level needed. For v0.1 (rendering only, no async NAPI), `napi4` may
be unnecessary overhead; `napi6` or `napi8` may be required for v3 features.
Defer to napi-rs v3 docs.

**Q5 — pipeline feature in npm package:** Does `packages/michi-node` expose
pipeline types to TypeScript? For v0.1: no. The npm package is rendering
primitives only. Pipeline execution in TypeScript consumers goes through the MCP
adapter layer, which is a Rust binary or sidecar, not a NAPI binding.

13	**Decision: one `michi` crate with optional features. No separate execution crate.**
14	
15	The original spec positioned michi as a pure sync rendering library with no
16	async runtime. The question was whether pipeline execution (tokio, moka, nucleo)
17	should live in a companion crate (`kata`) or in michi itself behind features.
18	
19	Feature gates give the same guarantee that crate boundaries give — a consumer
20	who adds `michi` with default features pulls in zero tokio, zero moka, zero
21	nucleo. The "pure computation" principle is enforced by cargo, not by convention.
22	
23	The suite tools (Monokl, Firkin, Lumen, Pulse) all need both rendering primitives
24	and pipeline execution. One crate means one dep, one version pin, one mental model.
25	Two crates would require cross-crate type conversions and coordinated releases with
26	no architectural benefit.
27	
28	The NAPI wrapper (`packages/michi-node`) remains a separate Cargo crate because
29	`crate-type = ["cdylib"]` cannot coexist with a regular `[lib]` in one
30	`Cargo.toml`. This is a build-artifact boundary, not a conceptual one.
31	
32	---
33	
34	## 2. Feature taxonomy
35	
36	```toml
37	[features]
38	default  = []
39	
40	# Async execution layer: PipelineExecutor, Step, CheckpointStore, OutputSink,
41	# CircuitBreaker, with_resilience(). Adds: tokio, tokio-util, async-trait,
42	# thiserror, uuid.
43	pipeline = [
44	    "dep:tokio",
45	    "dep:tokio-util",
46	    "dep:async-trait",
47	    "dep:uuid",
48	]
49	
50	# Fuzzy matching: FuzzyMatcher, FuzzyResolver, Disambiguator trait.
51	# Implies pipeline (Resolution<T> is used in pipeline context).
52	# Adds: nucleo-matcher.
53	fuzzy = ["dep:nucleo-matcher", "pipeline"]
54	
55	# Two-tier cache: moka async LRU + disk LRU with tag invalidation +
56	# stale-while-revalidate. Adds: moka, sha2.
57	cache = ["dep:moka", "dep:sha2", "pipeline"]
58	
59	# CLI surface adapter: CliSink (indicatif spinners), DiskCheckpointStore,
60	# TtyDisambiguator, install_ctrl_c_handler.
61	# Adds: indicatif, inquire, crossterm, ctrlc, atty.
62	cli = [
63	    "dep:indicatif",
64	    "dep:inquire",
65	    "dep:crossterm",
66	    "dep:ctrlc",
67	    "dep:atty",
68	    "pipeline",
69	]
70	
71	# MCP surface adapter: McpSink, MemoryCheckpointStore, McpDisambiguator.
72	# Pure logic — no additional non-tokio deps.
73	mcp = ["pipeline"]
74	
75	# NAPI npm wrapper surface. Used by packages/michi-node only.
76	napi = ["dep:napi", "dep:napi-derive"]
77	
78	# Everything except napi (napi is build-artifact-level, not feature-level).
79	full = ["pipeline", "fuzzy", "cache", "cli", "mcp"]
80	```
81	
82	Typical consumer configs:
83	
84	| Consumer | Features |
85	|---|---|
86	| Pure rendering (Rust CLI, no pipeline) | `michi` (defaults) |
87	| Rust CLI that runs pipelines | `michi = { features = ["cli"] }` |
88	| TypeScript MCP server via npm | `michi` npm package (default) |
89	| MCP server that runs pipelines | `michi = { features = ["mcp"] }` |
90	| Test/bench harness | `michi = { features = ["full"] }` |
91	| `packages/michi-node` Cargo.toml | `michi = { features = ["napi"] }` |
92	
93	---
94	
95	## 3. Module map
96	
97	Modules in the left column are always compiled (default features). Modules in
98	the right column are gated.
99	
100	```
101	src/
102	  lib.rs
103	
104	  ── Always compiled ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
105	
106	  toon/
107	    mod.rs          render_toon(), ToonOptions, Value
108	    escape.rs       comma/quote/null escaping
109	    render.rs       string assembly with pre-allocated capacity
110	
111	  kv/
112	    mod.rs          render_kv(), KvItem, KvValue
113	
114	  hints.rs          Hint, render_hints(), append_hints()
115	  truncate.rs       Truncated, truncate(), truncate_inline()
116	  empty.rs          empty_state(), empty_state_with_hints()
117	  error.rs          Error (unified — see §4), ErrorClass, Sensitive<T>
118	  idempotency.rs    IdempotencyKey, already_done(), PartialSuccess
119	  recovery.rs       RecoveryHint, render_recovery()
120	  status.rs         StatusItem, StatusResponse, Health
121	  response.rs       AgentResponse builder, OutputFormat
122	
123	  resilience/
124	    mod.rs          RetryConfig, next_retry_delay(), parse_retry_after()  ← always
125	    policy.rs       with_resilience()                                      ← pipeline
126	    circuit.rs      CircuitBreaker, CircuitState                          ← pipeline
127	
128	  pipeline/
129	    mod.rs          Pipeline (pure data type + render())                   ← always
130	    executor.rs     PipelineExecutor, PipelineContext                     ← pipeline
131	    step.rs         Step, StepFn, StepContext, SkipReason                 ← pipeline
132	    graph.rs        assign_levels(), cycle detection                      ← pipeline
133	    result.rs       PipelineResult, RunStatus                             ← pipeline
134	    checkpoint.rs   Checkpoint, CheckpointStore, NoopCheckpointStore      ← pipeline
135	
136	  sink/
137	    mod.rs          OutputSink, AgentEvent, NoopSink                      ← pipeline
138	
139	  telemetry/
140	    mod.rs          TelemetryProvider, NoopProvider                       ← always (zero-cost)
141	
142	  ── Optional features ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
143	
144	  fuzzy/
145	    mod.rs          FuzzyMatcher, FuzzyResolver, Resolution<T>            ← fuzzy
146	    matcher.rs      nucleo-matcher wrapper, MatcherConfig                 ← fuzzy
147	    resolver.rs     Disambiguator trait, resolve()                        ← fuzzy
148	
149	  cache/
150	    mod.rs          Cache, CachePolicy, CacheEntry                        ← cache
151	    memory.rs       moka::future::Cache wrapper                           ← cache
152	    disk.rs         DiskCache, tag invalidation                           ← cache
153	    policy.rs       CachePolicyBuilder, stale-while-revalidate            ← cache
154	
155	  adapters/
156	    cli/
157	      mod.rs        CliSink, HumanWriter, JsonWriter                      ← cli
158	      checkpoint.rs DiskCheckpointStore                                   ← cli
159	      disambig.rs   TtyDisambiguator                                      ← cli
160	      ctrl_c.rs     install_ctrl_c_handler()                              ← cli
161	    mcp/
162	      mod.rs        McpSink                                               ← mcp
163	      checkpoint.rs MemoryCheckpointStore                                 ← mcp
164	      disambig.rs   McpDisambiguator                                      ← mcp
165	
166	  napi.rs           #[napi] exports                                       ← napi
167	```
168	
169	### Module principles
170	
171	- Pure vs async split within a module: sync computation always compiled, async
172	  extension behind `pipeline`. Pattern from `resilience/`: `next_retry_delay()`
173	  is always there; `with_resilience()` requires the feature.
174	- `pipeline::Pipeline` (pure data type + `render()`) is always compiled because
175	  tools may want to render a pipeline state without executing it.
176	- `telemetry` uses `NoopProvider` (zero-cost impl) so it compiles clean without
177	  a runtime dep.
178	
179	---
180	
181	## 4. Error type consolidation
182	
183	The original spec had `AxiError` (rendering-focused, michi) as a separate concept
184	from `AgentError` (infrastructure, the proposed execution spec). In a unified
185	crate these merge into `michi::Error`.
186	
187	```rust
188	// src/error.rs
189	#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
190	pub enum Error {
191	    // ── Execution errors (pipeline feature) ───────────────────────────────
192	    #[error("HTTP {status}: {message}")]
193	    Http { status: u16, message: String, retryable: bool, retry_after: Option<Duration> },
194	
195	    #[error("Timeout after {elapsed:?}")]
196	    Timeout { elapsed: Duration },
197	
198	    #[error("Step {id} failed")]
199	    StepFailed { id: String, #[source] source: Box<Error> },
200	
201	    #[error("Circuit {name} is open, retry after {retry_after:?}")]
202	    CircuitOpen { name: String, retry_after: Duration },
203	
204	    #[error("No match for query: {query}")]
205	    NoMatch { query: String },
206	
207	    #[error("Ambiguous match for {query}: {count} candidates")]
208	    AmbiguousMatch { query: String, count: usize },
209	
210	    #[error("Cyclic dependency: {cycle:?}")]
211	    CyclicDependency { cycle: Vec<String> },
212	
213	    #[error("Cancelled")]
214	    Cancelled,
215	
216	    #[error("Cache error: {0}")]
217	    Cache(String),
218	
219	    #[error(transparent)]
220	    Io(#[from] std::io::Error),
221	
222	    // ── Domain errors (always) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
223	    #[error("Invalid input: {0}")]
224	    InvalidInput(String),
225	
226	    #[error("Not found: {0}")]
227	    NotFound(String),
228	}
229	
230	impl Error {
231	    /// Render to agent-readable stdout string (AxiError-style).
232	    pub fn render(&self) -> String { ... }
233	    pub fn exit_code(&self) -> i32 { 1 }
234	    pub fn class(&self) -> ErrorClass { ... }
235	    pub fn is_retryable(&self) -> bool { ... }
236	}
237	
238	pub enum ErrorClass { User, Internal, Transient }
239	
240	/// Wrapper that omits the inner value from Debug/Display output.
241	pub struct Sensitive<T>(pub T);
242	```
243	
244	`Sensitive<T>` and `ErrorClass` are always compiled. The execution error variants
245	(`Http`, `Timeout`, `StepFailed`, `CircuitOpen`, `NoMatch`, `AmbiguousMatch`,
246	`CyclicDependency`, `Cancelled`, `Cache`) are gated behind `#[cfg(feature = "pipeline")]`.
247	
248	---
249	
250	## 5. Repo shape
251	
252	```
253	michi/                          ← git root: git@github.com:orin-axi/michi.git
254	  Cargo.toml                    ← [workspace] members + [package] michi lib
255	  Cargo.lock
256	  rust-toolchain.toml           ← pinned stable channel
257	  build.rs                      ← napi-build (conditional on napi feature)
258	  justfile                      ← unified task runner (see §6)
259	  .rustfmt.toml                 ← edition=2021, max_width=120
260	  .clippy.toml                  ← msrv, too-many-arguments-threshold=6
261	  .typos.toml                   ← spell-check config
262	  deny.toml                     ← license + advisory + bans policy
263	  CLAUDE.md                     ← agent session instructions
264	  README.md
265	  src/                          ← michi lib source (as above)
266	  benches/
267	    toon_render.rs
268	    kv_render.rs
269	    pipeline_render.rs
270	  tests/
271	    toon_integration.rs
272	    kv_integration.rs
273	    resilience_integration.rs
274	    idempotency_integration.rs
275	    pipeline_integration.rs     ← pipeline feature, uses tokio::test
276	    snapshot_tests.rs           ← insta snapshots
277	  packages/
278	    michi-node/                 ← NAPI cdylib (separate Cargo crate, required by Rust)
279	      Cargo.toml                ← crate-type = ["cdylib"], deps on michi napi feature
280	      package.json              ← name: "michi", published to npm
281	      index.js                  ← platform binary loader
282	      index.d.ts                ← generated by napi-derive v3
283	      src/lib.rs                ← thin #[napi] shim over michi::*
284	      __test__/
285	        index.test.mjs
286	  .github/

300	**Workspace Cargo.toml:**

306	    "packages/michi-node",

332	## 6. Tooling stack
333	
334	| Tool | Role | Version |
335	|---|---|---|
336	| `just` | Unified local task runner | latest |
337	| `cargo nextest` | Parallel test runner (replaces `cargo test`) | via taiki-e/install-action |
338	| `cargo-llvm-cov` | Coverage → lcov → Codecov | via taiki-e/install-action |
339	| `cargo-deny` | License + advisory + ban policy | latest |
340	| `divan` | Benchmarks (not criterion) | 0.1 |
341	| `insta` | Snapshot tests | 1, yaml feature |
342	| `typos` | Spell-check | latest |
343	| `pnpm` | JS package manager for michi-node | 9+ |
344	| `@napi-rs/cli` | NAPI build + publish tooling | 3 |
345	| `napi` / `napi-derive` | NAPI bindings | **3** (not 2) |
346	
347	**Not used:**
348	- `criterion` — divan is the benchmark crate (consistent with oxc-react-codegen)
349	- `rayon` — pure sync rendering has no parallelism to exploit at the crate level
350	- `miette` — callers own error display; michi's error type focuses on agent rendering
351	- Moon — repo is too small; two crates don't need a polyglot task graph
352	- tokio in default features — execution layer is always opt-in via `pipeline` feature

384

386	check: fmt-check clippy deny typos
387

389	    cargo fmt --all
390	
391	fmt-check:
392	    cargo fmt --all --check
393	
394	clippy:
395	    cargo clippy --workspace --all-features -- -D warnings
396

398	    cargo deny check
399

402

404	snapshots:

406

408	bench:
409	    cargo bench --workspace
410	
411	# ── Coverage ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
412	coverage:
413	    cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --all-features --lcov --output-path lcov.info

417	```

423	## 7. Spec updates required in 01-spec.md
424	
425	These items in the existing spec are now outdated and should be corrected during
426	implementation:
427	
428	| Location | Current (wrong) | Correct |
429	|---|---|---|
430	| `Cargo.toml` `[dependencies.napi]` | `version = "2"` | `version = "3"` |
431	| `Cargo.toml` `[dependencies.napi-derive]` | `version = "2"` | `version = "3"` |
432	| `Cargo.toml` `[dev-dependencies]` | `criterion = { version = "0.5" }` | `divan = "0.1"` |
433	| `[features]` | `napi`, `cli = []` only | Full feature taxonomy (see §2) |
434	| Non-goals | "zero tokio, zero async-std" | True for default features; `pipeline` feature adds tokio |
435	| Consumer map | No pipeline mention | Add pipeline execution consumer shape |
436	| `error.rs` | `AxiError, ErrorCode` | `Error` (unified), `ErrorClass`, `Sensitive<T>` |
437	| `[[bench]]` | `harness = false` under criterion | divan bench setup |
438	
439	---
440	
441	## 8. Open questions (not blocking v0.1)
442	
443	**Q1 — MSRV:** Set to 1.96 in workspace (matching oxc-react-codegen pattern).
444	Verify no dep requires higher before first publish.
445	
446	**Q2 — disk cache path:** `DiskCache` needs a path at construction. CLI adapter
447	uses `~/.cache/michi/`. MCP adapter uses temp dir. Injected by the caller —
448	michi provides no default path discovery.
449	
450	**Q3 — AGPL vs MIT/Apache:** Spec says AGPL-3.0-or-later. Confirm with project
451	owner before publish. AGPL requires source disclosure for network use, which may
452	affect suite tool consumers.
453	
454	**Q4 — `napi4` feature level:** Spec historically chose `napi4` for
455	ThreadsafeFunction. With NAPI v3 and the sync-only default feature set, verify
456	the minimum level needed. For v0.1 (rendering only, no async NAPI), `napi4` may
457	be unnecessary overhead; `napi6` or `napi8` may be required for v3 features.
458	Defer to napi-rs v3 docs.
459	
460	**Q5 — pipeline feature in npm package:** Does `packages/michi-node` expose
461	pipeline types to TypeScript? For v0.1: no. The npm package is rendering
462	primitives only. Pipeline execution in TypeScript consumers goes through the MCP
463	adapter layer, which is a Rust binary or sidecar, not a NAPI binding.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/gabe/.claude/plugins/cache/superpowers-marketplace/superpowers/5.1.0/skills/writing-plans

# Writing Plans

## Overview

Write comprehensive implementation plans assuming the engineer has zero context for our codebase and questionable taste. Document everything they need to know: which files to touch for each task, code, testing, docs they might need to check, how to test it. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.

Assume they are a skilled developer, but know almost nothing about our toolset or problem domain. Assume they don't know good test design very well.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."

**Context:** If working in an isolated worktree, it should have been created via the `superpowers:using-git-worktrees` skill at execution time.

**Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`
- (User preferences for plan location override this default)

## Scope Check

If the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans — one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.

## File Structure

Before defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.

- Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.
- You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.
- Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.
- In existing codebases, follow established patterns. If the codebase uses large files, don't unilaterally restructure - but if a file you're modifying has grown unwieldy, including a split in the plan is reasonable.

This structure informs the task decomposition. Each task should produce self-contained changes that make sense independently.

## Bite-Sized Task Granularity

**Each step is one action (2-5 minutes):**
- "Write the failing test" - step
- "Run it to make sure it fails" - step
- "Implement the minimal code to make the test pass" - step
- "Run the tests and make sure they pass" - step
- "Commit" - step

## Plan Document Header

**Every plan MUST start with this header:**

```markdown
# [Feature Name] Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]

**Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]

**Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]

---
```

## Task Structure

````markdown
### Task N: [Component Name]

**Files:**
- Create: `exact/path/to/file.py`
- Modify: `exact/path/to/existing.py:123-145`
- Test: `tests/exact/path/to/test.py`

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

```python
def test_specific_behavior():
    result = function(input)
    assert result == expected
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Run test to verify it fails**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: FAIL with "function not defined"

- [ ] **Step 3: Write minimal implementation**

```python
def function(input):
    return expected
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Run test to verify it passes**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: PASS

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add tests/path/test.py src/path/file.py
git commit -m "feat: add specific feature"
```
````

## No Placeholders

Every step must contain the actual content an engineer needs. These are **plan failures** — never write them:
- "TBD", "TODO", "implement later", "fill in details"
- "Add appropriate error handling" / "add validation" / "handle edge cases"
- "Write tests for the above" (without actual test code)
- "Similar to Task N" (repeat the code — the engineer may be reading tasks out of order)
- Steps that describe what to do without showing how (code blocks required for code steps)
- References to types, functions, or methods not defined in any task

## Remember
- Exact file paths always
- Complete code in every step — if a step changes code, show the code
- Exact commands with expected output
- DRY, YAGNI, TDD, frequent commits

## Self-Review

After writing the complete plan, look at the spec with fresh eyes and check the plan against it. This is a checklist you run yourself — not a subagent dispatch.

**1. Spec coverage:** Skim each section/requirement in the spec. Can you point to a task that implements it? List any gaps.

**2. Placeholder scan:** Search your plan for red flags — any of the patterns from the "No Placeholders" section above. Fix them.

**3. Type consistency:** Do the types, method signatures, and property names you used in later tasks match what you defined in earlier tasks? A function called `clearLayers()` in Task 3 but `clearFullLayers()` in Task 7 is a bug.

# Subagent-Driven Development

Execute plan by dispatching fresh subagent per task, with two-stage review after each: spec compliance review first, then code quality review.

**Why subagents:** You delegate tasks to specialized agents with isolated context. By precisely crafting their instructions and context, you ensure they stay focused and succeed at their task. They should never inherit your session's context or history — you construct exactly what they need. This also preserves your own context for coordination work.

**Core principle:** Fresh subagent per task + two-stage review (spec then quality) = high quality, fast iteration

**Continuous execution:** Do not pause to check in with your human partner between tasks. Execute all tasks from the plan without stopping. The only reasons to stop are: BLOCKED status you cannot resolve, ambiguity that genuinely prevents progress, or all tasks complete. "Should I continue?" prompts and progress summaries waste their time — they asked you to execute the plan, so execute it.

## When to Use

```dot
}
```

**vs. Executing Plans (parallel session):**
- Same session (no context switch)
- Fresh subagent per task (no context pollution)
- Two-stage review after each task: spec compliance first, then code quality
- Faster iteration (no human-in-loop between tasks)

## Model Selection

Use the least powerful model that can handle each role to conserve cost and increase speed.

**Mechanical implementation tasks** (isolated functions, clear specs, 1-2 files): use a fast, cheap model. Most implementation tasks are mechanical when the plan is well-specified.

**Integration and judgment tasks** (multi-file coordination, pattern matching, debugging): use a standard model.

**Architecture, design, and review tasks**: use the most capable available model.

**Task complexity signals:**
- Touches 1-2 files with a complete spec → cheap model
- Touches multiple files with integration concerns → standard model
- Requires design judgment or broad codebase understanding → most capable model

## Handling Implementer Status

Implementer subagents report one of four statuses. Handle each appropriately:

**DONE:** Proceed to spec compliance review.

**DONE_WITH_CONCERNS:** The implementer completed the work but flagged doubts. Read the concerns before proceeding. If the concerns are about correctness or scope, address them before review. If they're observations (e.g., "this file is getting large"), note them and proceed to review.

**NEEDS_CONTEXT:** The implementer needs information that wasn't provided. Provide the missing context and re-dispatch.

**BLOCKED:** The implementer cannot complete the task. Assess the blocker:
1. If it's a context problem, provide more context and re-dispatch with the same model
2. If the task requires more reasoning, re-dispatch with a more capable model
3. If the task is too large, break it into smaller pieces
4. If the plan itself is wrong, escalate to the human

**Never** ignore an escalation or force the same model to retry without changes. If the implementer said it's stuck, something needs to change.

## Prompt Templates

- `./implementer-prompt.md` - Dispatch implementer subagent
- `./spec-reviewer-prompt.md` - Dispatch spec compliance reviewer subagent
- `./code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md` - Dispatch code quality reviewer subagent


## Advantages

**vs. Manual execution:**
- Subagents follow TDD naturally
- Fresh context per task (no confusion)
- Parallel-safe (subagents don't interfere)
- Subagent can ask questions (before AND during work)

**vs. Executing Plans:**
- Same session (no handoff)
- Continuous progress (no waiting)
- Review checkpoints automatic

**Efficiency gains:**
- No file reading overhead (controller provides full text)
- Controller curates exactly what context is needed
- Subagent gets complete information upfront
- Questions surfaced before work begins (not after)

**Quality gates:**
- Self-review catches issues before handoff
- Two-stage review: spec compliance, then code quality
- Review loops ensure fixes actually work
- Spec compliance prevents over/under-building
- Code quality ensures implementation is well-built

**Cost:**
- More subagent invocations (implementer + 2 reviewers per task)
- Controller does more prep work (extracting all tasks upfront)
- Review loops add iterations
- But catches issues early (cheaper than debugging later)

## Red Flags

**Never:**
- Start implementation on main/master branch without explicit user consent
- Skip reviews (spec compliance OR code quality)
- Proceed with unfixed issues
- Dispatch multiple implementation subagents in parallel (conflicts)
- Make subagent read plan file (provide full text instead)
- Skip scene-setting context (subagent needs to understand where task fits)
- Ignore subagent questions (answer before letting them proceed)
- Accept "close enough" on spec compliance (spec reviewer found issues = not done)
- Skip review loops (reviewer found issues = implementer fixes = review again)
- Let implementer self-review replace actual review (both are needed)
- **Start code quality review before spec compliance is ✅** (wrong order)
- Move to next task while either review has open issues

**If subagent asks questions:**
- Answer clearly and completely
- Provide additional context if needed
- Don't rush them into implementation

**If reviewer finds issues:**
- Implementer (same subagent) fixes them
- Reviewer reviews again
- Repeat until approved
- Don't skip the re-review

**If subagent fails task:**
- Dispatch fix subagent with specific instructions
- Don't try to fix manually (context pollution)

You are implementing Task 1: Repo scaffold for the `michi` Rust crate.

## Task Description

Create all scaffolding files for a new Rust workspace. Work in `/Users/gabe/Projects/michi`.

### CLAUDE.md

```markdown
# michi — Agent Instructions

## Commands
- `just test` — run all tests (Rust + Node)
- `just test-rust` — Rust tests only (cargo nextest)
- `just check` — fmt + clippy + deny + typos
- `just build-node` — compile NAPI binary for local platform
- `just bench` — run divan benchmarks
- `just snapshots` — review insta snapshot diffs
- `just coverage` — generate lcov.info

## Non-negotiables
- No `unwrap()`/`expect()` in lib code (tests OK with message)
- No `unsafe` outside napi boundary
- `BTreeMap` for output maps, `HashMap` for internal state only
- Pre-allocate strings with `String::with_capacity`
- Truncation uses char boundaries (`floor_char_boundary`)
- Every `pub` item has a doc comment
- NAPI: `version = "3"`, `#[napi(catch_unwind)]` on every export
- Benchmarks: divan (not criterion)
- Tests: `cargo nextest run` (not `cargo test`)

## Architecture
- `src/` — pure sync rendering library (default features: zero runtime deps)
- `packages/michi-node/` — thin NAPI cdylib shim, published as npm `michi`
- Feature flags: `pipeline` (tokio), `fuzzy`, `cache`, `cli`, `mcp`, `napi`
- See `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-03-michi-design.md` for decisions
- See `docs/01-spec.md` for full module API reference

## Module guide
| Module | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `toon` | TOON list rendering — token-optimized agent list format |
| `kv` | Key-value single-item rendering |
| `hints` | `help[]` hint blocks |
| `truncate` | Token-safe content truncation |
| `empty` | Definitive empty state responses |
| `error` | Unified `michi::Error` type with agent rendering |
| `idempotency` | Idempotency keys, already-done detection |
| `resilience` | Retry config, delay calculation, retry-after parsing |
| `status` | Health/status response rendering |
| `recovery` | Recovery hint blocks |
| `response` | `AgentResponse` builder — composes all primitives |
| `pipeline` | Pipeline pure data type + render (execution in Plan 2) |
```

## Context

This is a brand new repository. The `docs/` directory already exists at `/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/docs/` with spec files. The git repo does not exist yet — you need to `git init`.

```yaml
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  INSTA_UPDATE: "no"
  RUST_BACKTRACE: 1

jobs:
  lint:
    name: Lint
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: rustfmt, clippy
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - run: cargo fmt --all --check
      - run: cargo clippy --workspace --all-features -- -D warnings
      - name: typos
        uses: crate-ci/typos@master

  test:
    name: Test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@nextest
      - run: cargo nextest run --workspace
      - run: cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features

  deny:
    name: Deny
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny-action@v2

  coverage:
    name: Coverage
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: llvm-tools-preview
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@cargo-llvm-cov
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@nextest
      - run: cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --all-features --lcov --output-path lcov.info
      - uses: codecov/codecov-action@v4
        with:
          files: lcov.info
          fail_ci_if_error: false

  bench-build:
    name: Bench (build only)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - run: cargo bench --no-run --workspace

  napi:
    name: NAPI (${{ matrix.target }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - target: x86_64-apple-darwin
            runner: macos-13
          - target: aarch64-apple-darwin
            runner: macos-latest
          - target: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
            runner: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          targets: ${{ matrix.target }}
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 9
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: pnpm
          cache-dependency-path: packages/michi-node/pnpm-lock.yaml
      - run: pnpm install
        working-directory: packages/michi-node
      - run: pnpm build --target ${{ matrix.target }}
        working-directory: packages/michi-node
      - run: node --test __test__/index.test.mjs
        working-directory: packages/michi-node
        if: matrix.target != 'aarch64-apple-darwin'
```

Research the best lint rules and configurations for a high-quality Rust crate and its NAPI Node.js wrapper. I want a concrete, opinionated recommendation — not a dump of every lint that exists.

Context: We're building `michi`, a pure rendering primitives library (no async in default features). It has:
- A Rust lib crate (`src/`) — sync, no unsafe (except NAPI boundary), public API
- A NAPI v3 cdylib (`packages/michi-node/src/lib.rs`) — thin JS wrapper with `#[napi(catch_unwind)]` exports
- A JS test file (`__test__/index.test.mjs`) — no TypeScript source, just test

Current lint setup:
- `.clippy.toml`: `msrv = "1.96"`, `too-many-arguments-threshold = 6`, `too-many-lines-threshold = 150`
- `.rustfmt.toml`: `max_width = 120`, `use_small_heuristics = "Max"`
- `packages/michi-node/src/lib.rs`: `#![deny(clippy::all)]`
- No JS/TS linting at all

## Research tasks

1. **Clippy lint groups** — What's the current community consensus on `pedantic` / `nursery` / `restriction`? Which ones are worth enabling for a library vs an application? Look at what popular Rust projects do (tokio, axum, serde, rustfmt, etc.) — do they enable pedantic? What do they allow?

2. **Best per-lint recommendations** — From the `restriction` group, which individual lints are high-value for a library? Focus on:
   - Safety: `unwrap_used`, `expect_used`, `panic`, `todo`, `unimplemented`, `indexing_slicing`
   - Docs: `missing_errors_doc`, `missing_panics_doc`, `missing_docs_in_private_items`
   - Correctness: `use_self`, `needless_pass_by_value`, `implicit_clone`, `redundant_clone`
   - Performance: `string_to_string`, `inefficient_to_string`, `trivially_copy_pass_by_ref`
   - Readability: `semicolon_if_nothing_returned`, `items_after_statements`

3. **rustc lints** — What rustc-level warnings are worth promoting to errors for a library? (`missing_docs`, `unreachable_pub`, `unused_crate_dependencies`, etc.)

4. **NAPI-specific** — What lint rules make sense for NAPI cdylib code specifically? (E.g., always `catch_unwind`, no panics, no `u64` boundary, etc. — are there clippy rules that catch these?)

5. **JS/TS linting (oxlint)** — We only have `__test__/index.test.mjs`. Is oxlint the right choice? What's the minimal config that catches real bugs vs just style? What does a `package.json` `lint` script look like with oxlint?

## Output format

Structured recommendations I can implement directly:

### A. `src/lib.rs` crate-level attributes
```rust
// exact list with inline comments on why each is included
```

### B. `.clippy.toml` additions
```toml
// what to add
```

### C. NAPI crate (`packages/michi-node/src/lib.rs`) attributes
```rust

```

### D. oxlint setup
- Package to install, script entry in package.json
- Config file if needed
- What rules to enable

### E. CI impact
- Which of these will be caught by the existing `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features -- -D warnings` CI step?
- Anything that needs a separate CI step?

Keep it concise. I want actionable recommendations, not an exhaustive survey. Where there's a tradeoff, give me your opinion.

Here are my concrete, opinionated recommendations.

---

## What popular projects actually do

**Tokio, axum, rustfmt, serde**: None of them enable `clippy::pedantic` as a group wholesale. The pattern is `#![warn(clippy::all)]` plus a curated list of pedantic/restriction lints with explicit allows for the noise. That said, for a *library* with strict non-negotiables (no unwrap, all docs), enabling `pedantic` and suppressing the noise is the right call — you get strict defaults for future code.

**Nursery**: Don't enable. It's unstable, changes between Rust releases, and has high false-positive rates. Skip it entirely.

---

## A. `src/lib.rs` — crate-level attributes

Add this block at the top of `/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/src/lib.rs`:

```rust
// -- rustc lints ----------------------------------------------------------
#![warn(missing_docs)]           // enforces "every pub item has a doc comment" rule at CI
#![warn(unreachable_pub)]        // catches `pub` items not reachable from crate root → should be `pub(crate)`
#![warn(unused_qualifications)]  // simplify over-qualified paths (e.g. `std::string::String`)
#![warn(unused_lifetimes)]       // catches dead `'a` parameters

// -- clippy groups --------------------------------------------------------
#![warn(clippy::all)]            // the default correctness group (already implied, explicit is clearer)
#![warn(clippy::pedantic)]       // raise the bar; noisy ones suppressed below

// Pedantic allows — known false positives for this codebase
#![allow(clippy::module_name_repetitions)] // `toon::ToonOptions`, `toon::render_toon` is idiomatic Rust
#![allow(clippy::must_use_candidate)]      // rendering fns return String; callers decide whether to use it
#![allow(clippy::missing_errors_doc)]      // re-evaluate once all pub fns have # Errors sections

// -- clippy::restriction (not in any group, must be explicit) -------------
// Safety — these match the existing project non-negotiables
#![warn(clippy::unwrap_used)]
#![warn(clippy::expect_used)]
#![warn(clippy::panic)]
#![warn(clippy::todo)]
#![warn(clippy::unimplemented)]
#![warn(clippy::indexing_slicing)]  // use .get() with proper error handling

// String performance — matters for a rendering lib that builds lots of strings
#![warn(clippy::string_to_string)]      // .to_string() on String → .clone()
#![warn(clippy::inefficient_to_string)] // .to_string() on &str → .to_owned()

// Style
#![warn(clippy::use_self)] // use `Self` in impl blocks instead of the concrete type name
```

**One existing violation to fix first**: `src/resilience/mod.rs:50-53` has `as u64` / `as f64` casts on `u128` values. Pedantic fires `cast_possible_truncation` and `cast_precision_loss` here. Easiest fix: add `#[allow(clippy::cast_possible_truncation, clippy::cast_precision_loss)]` on that function body, or (better) bound the `u128` values with `u64::try_from(...).unwrap_or(u64::MAX)` before casting.

---

## B. `.clippy.toml` additions

Add to `/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/.clippy.toml`:

```toml
# Allow unwrap/expect in #[cfg(test)] code — idiomatic and saves hundreds of #[allow] attrs
allow-unwrap-in-tests  = true
allow-expect-in-tests  = true

# Lower complexity threshold slightly from the default of 25
cognitive-complexity-threshold = 20

# Ban debug/print macros in library code (requires clippy::disallowed_macros, which is in restriction)
# Add #![warn(clippy::disallowed_macros)] to src/lib.rs to activate this
disallowed-macros = [
    { path = "std::println", reason = "library code must not print; use structured output primitives" },
    { path = "std::eprintln", reason = "library code must not print to stderr" },
    { path = "std::dbg",     reason = "debug macro must not ship in library code" },
]
```

Then add `#![warn(clippy::disallowed_macros)]` to the restriction section in `src/lib.rs`.

---

## C. NAPI crate (`packages/michi-node/src/lib.rs`)

The key difference from the lib crate: a panic in NAPI code **crashes the Node.js process**, so panic-related lints are `deny`, not `warn`. The crate is thin glue, so pedantic isn't worth the cast noise from `i32 as usize` conversions.

```rust
#![deny(clippy::all)]

// Panics crash the Node process — these are hard errors, not warnings
#![deny(clippy::unwrap_used)]
#![deny(clippy::expect_used)]
#![deny(clippy::panic)]
#![deny(clippy::indexing_slicing)]

// Style (warn, not deny)
#![warn(clippy::use_self)]
#![warn(clippy::string_to_string)]
```

**No `missing_docs`** — this crate is `publish = false`, it's internal glue. No `pedantic` — the `i32 as i64` / `i32 as usize` casts in the NAPI boundary are intentional and would produce noisy false positives.

**NAPI-specific note on u64**: There's no clippy rule for this. napi-rs v3 simply won't compile if you put `u64` on an `#[napi]` export without the BigInt feature — the compiler catches it. Your existing code correctly uses `i32` throughout. No lint needed.

---

## D. oxlint setup

Yes, oxlint is the right choice here. ESLint is massively over-engineered for a single `.mjs` test file. oxlint runs in milliseconds, zero config required, and its defaults cover the real bugs.

**Install** (in `packages/michi-node/`):
```
pnpm add -D oxlint
```

**`package.json` script addition**:
```json
"lint": "oxlint --env node __test__/"
```

**Optional** `/Users/gabe/Projects/michi/packages/michi-node/.oxlintrc.json` — only needed if you want to override defaults:
```json
{
  "$schema": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oxc-project/oxc/main/npm/oxlint/configuration_schema.json",
  "env": { "node": true },
  "rules": {
    "eqeqeq": "error",
    "no-console": "off"
  }
}
```

oxlint enables "correctness" rules by default, which covers `no-unused-vars`, `no-undef`, `no-constant-condition`, and similar real bugs. The only thing worth explicitly setting is `eqeqeq` (always `===`) and turning `no-console` off since test output is expected.

**Don't** add ESLint, don't add Biome, don't add a TypeScript config — there's no TS source and the test file is simple enough that oxlint defaults are sufficient.

---

## E. CI impact

**Already covered by the existing** `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features -- -D warnings` **step**:
- All Rust lints above — `#![warn(...)]` in source + CI's `-D warnings` flag = errors in CI
- `.clippy.toml` config is picked up automatically by the clippy step
- The `disallowed-macros` check is activated the moment you add the `#![warn]` attr

**New CI step needed** — add to `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, either as a new job or inside the existing `napi` job:

```yaml
  lint-js:
    name: Lint (JS)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: packages/michi-node
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 9
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: pnpm
          cache-dependency-path: packages/michi-node/pnpm-lock.yaml
      - run: pnpm install
      - run: pnpm lint
```

**Nothing else needs a separate step** — deny, typos, coverage, and bench already have their own jobs.

---

## Implementation order

1. `.clippy.toml` additions first (no source changes, non-breaking)
2. Add restriction lints to `packages/michi-node/src/lib.rs` — should pass immediately
3. Fix the resilience casts, then add the `src/lib.rs` crate attrs — run `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features` locally to see what breaks
4. Add oxlint + CI step

The pedantic enable will produce a small batch of violations on first run (mainly the resilience casts and possibly some `missing_errors_doc` gaps). Treat them as a one-time cleanup rather than a reason to skip pedantic.</result>

## oxlint Type-Aware Linting: Current State (July 2026)

### 1. Status: Alpha, powered by tsgolint (not tsserver)

Type-aware linting in oxlint is **alpha** as of December 2025. The underlying technology is **tsgolint** — a Go binary that runs the TypeScript 7 Go port (`typescript-go` / tsgo) to build TypeScript programs and execute type-aware rules. It is NOT tsserver and NOT oxlint's own type inference.

- oxlint v1.0 (stable, no type-aware) shipped June 2025
- Technical preview: August 2025
- Alpha (with rule config, inline disables, `--fix`): December 2025
- Current rule coverage: **59 out of 61** typescript-eslint type-aware rules
- Performance: ~10–20x faster than `eslint` + `typescript-eslint`
- Known limitation: memory pressure on very large monorepos; not a problem for a single-package repo like `michi-node`

**Required extra package:**
```bash
npm add -D oxlint-tsgolint@latest
```

Sources: [Type-Aware Alpha blog](https://oxc.rs/blog/2025-12-08-type-aware-alpha), [VoidZero announcement](https://voidzero.dev/posts/announcing-oxlint-type-aware-linting-alpha), [tsgolint GitHub](https://github.com/oxc-project/tsgolint)

---

### 2. CLI flags — what to use

| Flag | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `--type-aware` | Enable type-aware lint rules (the main switch) |
| `--type-check` | Emit TypeScript compiler diagnostics alongside lint (experimental — can replace `tsc --noEmit`) |
| `--tsconfig <path>` | Override tsconfig for **import resolution only** — NOT for type-aware; tsgolint auto-discovers tsconfig |

The docs explicitly warn: **do not rely on `--tsconfig` for type-aware linting** — tsgolint walks up the directory tree to find `tsconfig.json` automatically, and `--tsconfig` does not affect it.

---

### 3. .mjs file support — the critical question

Oxlint lists `.mjs` as a lintable extension (for standard rules). For type-aware rules via tsgolint, the docs use TypeScript file examples exclusively and **do not explicitly document .mjs support**.

The practical answer, based on how it works:

- tsgolint builds a TypeScript program using `typescript-go`. That program's scope is determined by your `tsconfig.json`.
- If your `tsconfig.json` has `"allowJs": true` and the `include` array covers `__test__/**/*.mjs`, then the `.mjs` file will be in the TypeScript program and tsgolint will apply type-aware rules to it.
- Without `allowJs: true`, the `.mjs` file is **not part of the TypeScript program** and gets no type-aware rules.

**You do not need to convert `index.test.mjs` to `.ts`** — but you do need `allowJs: true` in tsconfig.

---

### 4. Minimal `tsconfig.json` for `packages/michi-node/`

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2022",
    "module": "NodeNext",
    "moduleResolution": "NodeNext",
    "allowJs": true,
    "checkJs": true,
    "strict": true,
    "noEmit": true
  },
  "include": [
    "__test__/**/*",
    "index.d.ts"
  ]
}
```

Key decisions:
- `allowJs: true` — lets tsgolint (and tsc) include the `.mjs` test file
- `checkJs: true` — makes `tsc --noEmit` actually type-check the JS file (otherwise it's parse-only)
- `module: "NodeNext"` + `moduleResolution: "NodeNext"` — correct for Node.js 18+ ESM
- `include` covers only the test file and the generated `.d.ts`, not `index.js` (the binary loader, which is boilerplate)
- No `baseUrl` — removed in TypeScript 7; tsgolint requires TypeScript 7+ compatibility
- TypeScript 7 (tsgo) is what tsgolint uses internally; your installed `typescript` dev dep should be 7.x for consistency

---

### 5. Should you use `--type-check` or keep a separate `tsc --noEmit`?

**Recommendation: keep both, with oxlint handling rules and tsc handling diagnostics.**

`--type-check` (which makes oxlint emit tsc diagnostics) is still experimental. For a NAPI package where type correctness matters, use a separate `tsc --noEmit` until `--type-check` exits alpha. The two are complementary:

- `oxlint --type-aware` catches semantic issues (unhandled promises, unsafe member access, deprecated APIs) fast
- `tsc --noEmit` is the authoritative type-correctness check

This is the current community consensus — oxlint for speed + tsc for correctness. Blog posts and the oxlint docs both frame `--type-check` as a future replacement, not a current one.

---

### 6. Recommended `package.json` scripts

```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "lint": "oxlint --type-aware .",
    "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit",
    "check": "npm run typecheck && npm run lint"
  }
}
```

If you want to try the experimental combined mode:
```json

  "lint": "oxlint --type-aware --type-check ."
}
```
But `--type-check` is explicitly labeled experimental, so keep `tsc --noEmit` in CI until it stabilizes.

| Production-ready? | Alpha (December 2025) — stable for small repos, known memory issues at scale |
| Best practice combo | `oxlint --type-aware` + `tsc --noEmit` as separate scripts |</result>

1	# michi — Overview
2	
3	> orin-axi · Draft · June 2026
4	
5	---
6	
7	## What it is
8	
9	`michi` is a Rust crate of pure agentic response primitives — the formatting and signalling
10	conventions that make tools ergonomic for LLMs regardless of protocol or language. It is the
11	primitive layer of the **orin-axi** suite, encoding the [AXI](https://axi.md) (Agent eXperience
12	Interface) design principles as typed, tested Rust.
13	
14	AXI is a set of ten design principles for agent-ergonomic tooling that treats token budget as a
15	first-class constraint. Of the ten, michi encodes **seven** directly: TOON list rendering (P1),
16	content truncation (P3), pre-computed aggregates (P4), definitive empty states (P5), structured
17	errors with exit codes (P6), content-first status responses (P8), and contextual disclosure via
18	`help[]` blocks (P9). It also ships supporting idempotency and retry-delay primitives. The
19	remaining three principles (P2, P7, P10) depend on integration that michi deliberately excludes.
20	
21	The crate is intentionally narrow: **no protocol knowledge, no async runtime, no CLI framework**.
22	Pure computation — data in, strings and types out. TypeScript consumers reach it via the NAPI npm
23	wrapper `michi`; Rust consumers take a direct crates.io or git dependency.
24	
25	---
26	
27	## Quick start
28	
29	The same primitives, from either language. (Illustrative — see `docs/01-spec.md` for the precise
30	API.)
31	
32	```rust
33	use michi::toon;
34	
35	#[derive(serde::Serialize)]
36	struct Issue {
37	    number: u64,
38	    title: String,
39	    state: String,
40	}
41	
42	let issues = vec![
43	    Issue { number: 51815, title: "[Bug]: Telegram plugin".into(), state: "open".into() },
44	    Issue { number: 51812, title: "dark mode request".into(), state: "open".into() },
45	];
46	
47	// TOON list, an inline total count, and a next-step hint.
48	let response = toon::list("issues", &issues)
49	    .total(8771)
50	    .hint("gh-axi issue view <number>", "view an issue")
51	    .render();
52	
53	print!("{response}");
54	```
55	
56	```typescript
57	import { toon } from "michi";
58	
59	const issues = [
60	  { number: 51815, title: "[Bug]: Telegram plugin", state: "open" },
61	  { number: 51812, title: "dark mode request", state: "open" },
62	];
63	
64	// Identical primitives, via the NAPI wrapper.
65	const response = toon
66	  .list("issues", issues)
67	  .total(8771)
68	  .hint("gh-axi issue view <number>", "view an issue")
69	  .render();
70	
71	process.stdout.write(response);
72	```
73	
74	Both produce the same token-efficient output:
75	
76	```text
77	count: 2 of 8771 total
78	issues[2]{number,title,state}:
79	  51815,"[Bug]: Telegram plugin",open
80	  51812,dark mode request,open
81	help[1]:
82	  Run `gh-axi issue view <number>` to view an issue
83	```
84	
85	---
86	
87	## Name
88	
89	**michi** — from 道 (Japanese: path, way, road).
90	
91	The character 道 is the root of *dō* in martial arts and traditional arts: judo, kendo, aikido,
92	shodō, chadō. It means the path itself — and the act of travelling it with intention. In the
93	context of this crate, every `help[]` block is michi: a marker that tells an agent which path to
94	take next, with what parameters.
95	
96	Fits the suite's naming aesthetic: short real words borrowed from a specific domain, with a
97	metaphor that earns its place.
98	
99	| Name      | Origin          | Meaning                       |
100	| --------- | --------------- | ----------------------------- |
101	| Lumen     | Latin           | unit of luminous flux; light  |
102	| Firkin    | Middle English  | small barrel; a measured unit |
103	| Monokl    | Slavic / French | monocle; single-eye focus     |
104	| Pulse     | Latin           | vital sign; rhythmic signal   |
105	| **michi** | Japanese (道)   | path, way, road               |
106	
107	---
108	
109	## Organisation
110	
111	GitHub org: **orin-axi** (`github.com/orin-axi`)
112	
113	> "AXI" = Agent eXperience Interface. The orin-axi org is the umbrella for tools designed to serve
114	> both human developers and AI agents as first-class users. `michi` is the primitive layer — the
115	> shared vocabulary of agent responses that all other tools in the suite can build on.
116	
117	---
118	
119	## Where michi fits in the suite
120	
121	michi sits below every other tool in the orin-axi suite as the shared primitive layer. Each
122	agent-facing tool imports it rather than re-implementing AXI formatting.
123	
124	| Tool      | What it does                               | Uses michi for           |
125	| --------- | ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------ |
126	| **michi** | AXI response primitives — the shared layer | — (this crate)           |
127	| Monokl    | AST-based semantic code search             | TOON list output         |
128	| Firkin    | Barrel / index file generator              | Structured error output  |
129	| Lumen     | Coding-session analysis + ambient context  | Status + hint primitives |
130	| Pulse     | Code-health intelligence                   | TOON list output         |
131	
132	Non-agentic infrastructure tools (build scripts, formatters, etc.) never encounter michi — the
133	package boundary enforces the separation.
134

137	## AXI principles encoded
138	
139	| Principle                           | Module       | What michi provides                               | Status  |
140	| ----------------------------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------- | ------- |
141	| P1 — Token-efficient output         | `toon`       | TOON list rendering (~40% fewer tokens than JSON) | Encoded |
142	| P2 — Minimal default schemas        | `toon`, `kv` | Compact rendering; field names stated once        | Caller  |
143	| P3 — Content truncation             | `truncate`   | Size-bounded fields with `--full` escape hatch    | Encoded |
144	| P4 — Pre-computed aggregates        | `toon`, `kv` | Inline `totalCount` on every list and item        | Encoded |
145	| P5 — Definitive empty states        | `empty`      | Explicit `count: 0` message — never silent        | Encoded |
146	| P6 — Structured errors & exit codes | `error`      | Typed TOON errors on stdout; clean exit codes     | Encoded |
147	| P7 — Ambient context                | `status`     | `StatusResponse` payload for session dashboards   | Caller  |
148	| P8 — Content first                  | `status`     | Live-state response for no-arg invocations        | Encoded |
149	| P9 — Contextual disclosure          | `hints`      | `help[]` blocks of concrete next-step templates   | Encoded |
150	| P10 — Consistent way to get help    | —            | Per-subcommand `--help` reference contract        | Caller  |
151	
152	michi encodes **seven** principles directly — P1, P3, P4, P5, P6, P8, and P9 — as typed, tested
153	Rust, alongside supporting idempotency and retry-delay primitives (`idempotency`) that underpin
154	P6's robustness guarantees and make combined operations safe to retry.
155	
156	The remaining three are the **caller's responsibility**, because each requires integration michi
157	deliberately omits:
158	
159	- **P2 — Minimal default schemas** — michi renders any schema compactly, but the caller chooses
160	  which fields to expose by default and which to gate behind a `--fields` flag.
161	- **P7 — Ambient context** — michi produces the `StatusResponse` payload, but installing it into
162	  per-session hooks or a plugin system requires a CLI/agent harness.
163	- **P10 — Consistent way to get help** — routing per-subcommand `--help` is a CLI-framework
164	  concern, outside a pure primitives crate.
